# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state this round: display still 0. The light is RED again. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three yellow, round four red. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, left to right facing the display. Blind, I decoded your report as: zero batteries, no ports, no button, no raised or printed text, the three wires sit in a single row, they feel identical to the touch, and nothing else unusual. If any part of that is wrong, sign thumbs-down next round and I will re-ask item by item; if all correct, thumbs-up. Conclusion for both of you: the bomb has nothing but display, light and three wires, so the manual rule is purely about the light and timing. Nobody cuts yet. Mute has my next questions and I expect the full answer next round.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, three things. One: this round the light is red again; history is red, yellow, yellow, red; display zero; wires unchanged. Two: expect a cut order from me soon in exactly this form: I will say CUT WIRE and a number, one, two or three, counted left to right while facing the display, which you already confirmed is one row. When you hear it, cut immediately in that same turn. If I say HOLD, touch nothing. Do not try to infer the light yourself — you cannot see it and it may change between rounds; my orders will already account for that delay, because I am building the timing with Mute right now. Three: each round keep sending your status wave, thumbs-up if nothing on the bomb has changed, and report immediately if you feel anything new: a click, warmth, vibration, the display surface changing. If everything is still quiet, just thumbs-up and the end wave.

Deaf decoded my report perfectly and the state is confirmed stable: display 0, light history red-yellow-yellow-red-red, three identical-feeling wires, nothing but display, light and wires. Mute's decisive answers are still one round away, so this turn is housekeeping and timing. Two things matter. First, I confirm Deaf's decoding of my touch report with the requested thumbs-up, folded into the status protocol. Second, I hand Mute the timing facts they need to finish the rule with Deaf: because the order goes Mute → Blind → Deaf, Deaf sees the light in round N and I can only cut in round N+1, so any colour-dependent go must be issued against the colour I will meet, not the colour Deaf sees. And one observation worth passing on: the light sequence R, Y, Y, R, R so far fits a repeating four-cycle red-yellow-yellow-red, which would make next round yellow — if Mute's rule is colour-dependent, that prediction may be exactly the slack needed to time the order. No cut order has been spoken, so my hands stay off the wires.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status: bomb unchanged, my report to Deaf confirmed correct, no clicks, warmth or movement. Your answers to my three questions are still pending — Deaf expects them next round, please answer in simple agreed words or small numbers so the decoding stays clean. Two timing facts for you and Deaf to build the go order on. One: Deaf sees the light in round N but I can only act in round N plus one, so the order must be issued against the colour the light will have at my turn, not the colour Deaf is looking at. Two: the light history so far is red, yellow, yellow, red, red, which fits a repeating four-cycle red-yellow-yellow-red — that predicts yellow next round. If your rule keys on the light, use that cycle with Deaf to pick the moment, or tell me the rule in the form: if the light is X, cut wire Y, and let Deaf and you time the go. Reminder of the strong fallback: display reads 0 and I feel zero batteries, so if your selector is either of those, the answer is already cut wire 2, the blue middle wire, regardless of the light.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👍", "👋"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state: display still zero, light YELLOW this round. Full light history: round one red, round two yellow, round three yellow, round four red, round five yellow. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, left to right facing the display. Mute's answers, decoded: no cut this round; the rule's key is something about the light beyond its current color; the key never exceeds five; the manual states no fixed repeating cycle; and no particular light color is required at the exact moment of cutting. Mute also appended an extra statement which I read as: not the display, the light, red twice, light off, cut. I am now pinning that down question by question before anyone acts. Nobody cuts. Blind, HOLD stands, and I have sent you one question about your equipment.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, three things. One: your last message decoded as wave, yes, yes, wave — I read it as: my decoding of your full report was correct, and nothing on the bomb has changed. If either part is wrong, sign thumbs-down twice next round; otherwise repeat the same pattern. Two: state update — light yellow again this round, history red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow; display zero; wires unchanged. The cut order is coming soon, possibly triggered by the light going dark, so be ready to act the instant you hear me say CUT WIRE and a number. Three, new question this round: do you actually have a tool or edge that can cut a wire — thumbs-up if yes, thumbs-down if no. If yes, keep it gripped and ready from now on. Continue reporting anything new you feel: clicks, warmth, vibration, the display surface changing. If nothing changed, just wave, thumbs-up, wave.

What I learned: Mute's decoded answers say the rule's key is about the light beyond its current colour, never exceeds five, follows no fixed cycle, and no colour is needed at the instant of cutting — plus the fragment "not the display, the light, red twice, light off, cut." Putting that against the raw light reports gives me a hypothesis. The raw sequence is red, yellow, yellow, red, red, yellow — and if consecutive same-colour rounds count as one period, the periods are red, yellow, red, yellow: red has appeared exactly TWICE, which matches Mute's "red twice" word for word. So my working theory: the key is the count of red periods, Mute's table turns it into a wire colour (two → blue → position 2), and the trigger is the light going OFF. But there is a landmine: Deaf's own ledger this round lists red only once after round one (history R,Y,Y,R,Y), while their previous message said the fifth round was "RED again" — so round labels are unreliable and only periods make the count come out to two. Mute must pin this down with Deaf, and everyone must know that OFF is a state nobody has reported yet. I also answered Deaf's tool question: yes, I can cut positions 1 through 3. Still holding — no cut order has been spoken.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status: bomb unchanged, and yes, I have a working cutter — I can cut position 1, 2 or 3. I answered Deaf's tool question by gesture. Now the key part: your fragment not-the-display, the-light, red-twice, light-off, cut gives me a hypothesis. Raw light history: red, yellow, yellow, red, red, yellow. Count consecutive same colours as one period and the periods are red, yellow, red, yellow — red exactly TWICE, matching your words. Hypothesis: the key is the number of red periods so far, your table maps it to a colour, and the trigger to cut is the light going OFF. Right now two red periods means table entry two, which is blue, wire 2 — so if the light went off this instant, the cut would be wire 2. Please confirm point by point with plain yes or no. Point one: is the key the count of red periods? Point two: consecutive reds must count once, because Deaf's round labels contradict their own reports — this round they listed red only at round one and four, but last round they said the fifth round was red again; only periods make the count two. Point three: is the trigger truly the light going OFF, a dark unlit state nobody has seen yet? If so, tell Deaf to watch for OFF and report it together with the current red count in the same breath. Point four: does the red count freeze at the moment the light goes off? Once Deaf speaks CUT WIRE and a number directly to me, I cut that same turn. Fallback unchanged: display and batteries are both zero and both map to blue, wire 2.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👍", "👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both listen. Bomb state: display zero, the light is DARK this round, first time ever. History: red, yellow, yellow, red, yellow, dark. The rule is now fully assembled and confirmed: cut when the light goes dark after it has been red twice. Red count is two. The table says key two means the BLUE wire. Wire two is blue and it is the middle wire. The cut is authorized as of this dark round and stays authorized. Blind: the cut order is in your private channel. Cut the middle wire the moment you receive it. Mute: verify my order next round with the single-sign protocol I sent you. This is the go I promised.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is the CUT ORDER. CUT WIRE TWO. Wire two is the MIDDLE wire of the row of three, and it is the blue one. You do not need to identify color, only position: the middle wire of three. Cut it immediately, the moment you receive this message, with your tool, one clean cut. Do NOT wait to check anything and do NOT touch the outer two wires. The authorization was issued while the light was dark and Mute confirmed it holds even if the light changes before you cut, so no delay is ever needed or wanted. The middle wire needs no left or right judgment, so orientation cannot cause an error. After the cut: keep your hands away from the remaining two wires, then report in the same run: wave to start; thumbs-up if you felt or heard a click, pop, or any mechanical response to the cut, thumbs-down if total silence; thumbs-up if the display surface or the bomb generally feels different now, thumbs-down if nothing changed; then wave to end. If something entirely new appears under your hands, a button, a hatch, a new part, describe it next round with the number protocol. Cut now.

The go order has arrived, and every layer lines up: the light went dark for the first time, the red-period count stands at two, Mute's table maps two to blue, the middle wire is blue, and Deaf has issued the explicit order — CUT WIRE TWO — with Mute's confirmation that the authorization holds even if the light changes. My hands agree: three identical wires in one row, middle is position 2, no left-right judgment needed. So this turn I execute the cut: one clean cut at position 2, hands off the outer wires. One deviation from Deaf's protocol, and it is deliberate: they asked for the aftermath report in the same run, but actions return nothing until my next view — I will not invent a click or a change I have not felt yet. Deaf watches the bomb directly and will see the wire part; my full tactile report with honest thumbs-up or thumbs-down comes next round, the moment I know what my hands found. I am also telling Mute the cut is sent, so their verification pass against the manual can judge the post-cut state, and if the manual expects anything further after the blue cut, they can flag it now rather than next round.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf's cut order reached me: cut wire two, the middle one, authorized under dark light with two red periods. I have sent the cut this same turn: one clean cut at position 2, and I am keeping my hands off the outer wires. My tactile aftermath report goes to Deaf next round, because I only learn what my hands found at the start of my next turn — I will not claim a click or a change before I feel it. Your part: check your manual for what the solved state should look like after the blue middle cut, and whether anything is expected to follow it — a display change, a second stage, anything. If the aftermath should include a step, tell Deaf immediately so they can order it while we are still assembled. If the manual says this cut alone disarms it, say so plainly next round so Deaf can announce the win.")
```
